title: Verifying Installation and Status Codes
instructions: Use the newly installed `requests` library to fetch a test page and verify the HTTP status code. You'll need to run the `pip install requests` command in your environment before attempting the code exercise.
steps: Ensure you have run `pip install requests` in your active environment (this is a setup step, not a code step).
Make a GET request to the URL `https://httpbin.org/status/200`. Store the response object in a variable named `r_success`.
Make another GET request to the URL `https://httpbin.org/status/404`. Store the response object in a variable named `r_fail`.
starterCode:
import requests

# 1. Successful request (Status 200)
r_success = ...
print(f"Success Status: {r_success.status_code}")

# 2. Failing request (Status 404)
r_fail = ...
print(f"Failure Status: {r_fail.status_code}")
solution:
import requests

# 1. Successful request (Status 200)
r_success = requests.get('https://httpbin.org/status/200')
print(f"Success Status: {r_success.status_code}")

# 2. Failing request (Status 404)
r_fail = requests.get('https://httpbin.org/status/404')
print(f"Failure Status: {r_fail.status_code}")
hints: Remember to use `requests.get()` to make a GET request.
The status code is accessed using the `.status_code` property of the response object.
